operations.name: John Pacheta

expected.name: John Pacheta
expected.description: John Pacheta was prosecuted under United States wartime statutes of the World War I era (chiefly the Espionage Act, the Sedition Act, or the Selective Service Act). Recorded offense: Espionage Act (Title I), Section 3. Sentence: 2 years. Sentenced June 6, 1918. This case is documented in the 1921 U.S. Senate hearing "Amnesty and Pardon for Political Prisoners" (digitized by the Internet Archive).
expected.body:
1920s custody review: The 1921 Senate hearing, printed page 87, records June 6, 1918 as sentencing, not actual admission, and states that John Pacheta was transferred to St. Elizabeths on June 9, 1919. A hospital transfer is not release from custody. The previous June 6, 1920 release was sentence-length arithmetic, not a documented discharge. Sentencing is recorded separately and the unsupported admission/release endpoints and duration are cleared. The actual arrest, initial admission, hospital discharge and an identifiable photograph remain unresolved.

Source: 1921 Senate hearing, printed page 87, original table visually inspected.
